title: A Private Conversation
keyStructures: Statement order: Subject + Verb + Object + Manner + Place + Time. Note: 'Time' can also appear before the subject.
specialDifficulties: Statement word order: 'They are talking to my cat loudly in the kitchen yesterday'.

title: Breakfast or Lunch!
keyStructures: Simple Present (S + V1) vs. Simple Present Progressive (S + V1 + ing - can also indicate a plan). Stative Verbs (love, want, need, see, smell, etc.) cannot be used in Progressive form.
specialDifficulties: Exclamatory sentences: 'It is a terrible day!' vs. 'What a terrible day it is!'.

title: Please Send Me a Card
keyStructures: Simple Past Tense (S + V2) for actions completed in the past at a definite time, or past habits ('She never carried an umbrella', 'I used to eat a lot').
specialDifficulties: Direct and Indirect Objects: 'He lent me a book' vs. 'He lent a book to me'.

title: An Exciting Trip
keyStructures: Present Perfect (S + have/has + V3) for actions in indefinite time, actions repeating in the past, or starting in past and continuing now. Present Perfect Progressive (S + have/has + been + V1-ing) for expect, hope, learn, lie, look, sleep, sit, study, teach, stay, wait, work. Features: since, for, just, already, never, ever, lately, so far, yet, now.
specialDifficulties: Differences between 'receive' (menerima) and 'take' (mengambil).

title: No Wrong Numbers
keyStructures: Simple Past (completed, definite time: 'I drank coffee this morning') vs. Present Perfect (indefinite, recent: 'I have just opened the door').
specialDifficulties: Way idioms: 'in the way' (blocking), 'on the way' (di jalan), 'in this way' (specific way), 'by the way' (omong-omong), 'in a way' (bagaimanapun juga). Differences between 'spare' (meluangkan, cadangan) and 'to spare' (diluangkan, free time).

title: Percy Buttons
keyStructures: Particles: 'A' vs. 'Some' (a glass of milk vs. some milk), 'A' vs. 'The' (a man vs. the man). Names don't need particles. Specific information uses particles; common information does not.
specialDifficulties: Simple idioms: 'put on' (memakai), 'put off' (menunda), 'look after' (merawat). Knock idioms: 'knock down' (merobohkan), 'knock at' (mengetok), 'knock out' (mengalahkan), 'knock off' (menjatuhkan), 'knock over' (menyenggol).

title: Too Late
keyStructures: Past Progressive (S + was/were + V1-ing) for interrupted past actions, simultaneous past actions, or action at a specific past time. Note: 'When' before past simple, 'While' before past progressive.
specialDifficulties: Phrasal verb word order: 'He took off his coat' vs. 'He took his coat off'.

title: The Best and the Worst
keyStructures: Comparative and Superlative (..er than / more .. than vs. the ..est / the most ..). Examples: 'He is taller than she is', 'They are the most diligent students'.
specialDifficulties: Indefinite pronouns ('Everybody, everyone, everything') are always singular. Meanings of 'enter': come in, submit, enroll, etc.

title: A Cold Welcome
keyStructures: Prepositions of Time: 'At' (specific time), 'In' (general/longer period like month, year, season), 'On' (day, date, special days), 'Until', 'From', 'During', 'Till'.
specialDifficulties: Negative and non-assertive words: 'Any' vs. 'No' ('Is there anyone in the kitchen?' -> 'There isn't anyone' / 'There is no one in the kitchen').

title: Not For Jazz
keyStructures: Passive Voice: Present/Past Tense (to be/was/were + V3), Present/Past Progressive (to be/was/were + being + V3), Present/Past Perfect (has/have/had + been + V3), Modals (modal + be + V3).
specialDifficulties: 'Made in' (country), 'made of' (material), 'made from' (a number of materials), 'made by' (someone). Double genitive: 'He is one of my father's friends' -> 'He is a friend of my father's'.

title: One Good Turn Deserves Another
keyStructures: Combination of Key Structures: Mixing simple present, simple past, present perfect, past perfect, progressive tenses, and passive voice.
specialDifficulties: Applying correct tense harmony across complex sentences.

title: Good Bye and Good Luck
keyStructures: Simple Future: 'Will/shall + V1' (plan/decision) vs. 'Be going to + V1' (on the way to do it/intention).
specialDifficulties: Set idioms: 'Set up' (make/establish), 'set off' (starting a journey), 'set out' (arrange/begin an undertaking).

title: The Greenwood Boys
keyStructures: Future Progressive (will/shall + be + V1-ing) for action starting before specific future time ('I will be eating at 7 tomorrow'). Future Perfect (will/shall + have + V3) for action completed by a future time ('I will have graduated in AEC in 3 months' time').
specialDifficulties: Expressing possession in questions: 'Whose bike is it?' -> 'It is Ali's' or 'It belongs to Ali'.

title: Do You Speak English?
keyStructures: Past Perfect (S + had + V3) to indicate action completed before another past action ('I had had my breakfast before I went to school') or a state continuing for a time in the past ('I had lived in Soreang for 10 years before I moved').
specialDifficulties: Tense matching in complex narrative sentences.

title: Good News
keyStructures: Indirect Speech (Reported Speech): Tense changes (Simple Present -> Simple Past, Present Continuous -> Past Continuous, Simple Past -> Past Perfect, Future Simple -> Conditional Type 2). Command reporting (Clean your room! -> She told me to clean my room; Don't smoke here! -> She told me not to smoke here). Question reporting: He asked me what my name was (Wh- question); He asked if my name was Denaz (Auxiliary/Yes-No question). Time shifts (today -> that day, yesterday -> the day before, tomorrow -> the next day, etc.).
specialDifficulties: Word nuances: 'Nervous' (uneasy), 'Irritable' (easily made angry), 'afford' (be able to pay/do), 'office/desk/study' (study room vs workspace).

title: A Polite Request
keyStructures: Conditional Sentences: Type 0 (Habitual: If + Present, + Present), Type 1 (Probability: If + Present, + Future Simple), Type 2 (Impossible: If + Past, + Would + V1), Type 3 (Regret: If + Past Perfect, + Would Have + V3).
specialDifficulties: Recognizing inversion and correct modal selections in conditions.

title: Always Young
keyStructures: Modal verbs: 'Must' cannot be used in simple past (use 'had to' instead). Using 'must' for opinion/deduction ('I think he is tired -> He must be tired'). Difference between 'Grow' (quantity, plants) and 'Grow Up' (mind, maturity, values).
specialDifficulties: Usages of the word 'As' (representing Position, Similarity, Time Conjunction, Reason Conjunction, or 'Like'). Differences between 'Dress', 'Suit' (one package), and 'Costume' (themed clothing).

title: He Often Does This!
keyStructures: Usages of Have/Has/Had: 1) As auxiliary verb in perfect tenses ('Have you eaten?'); 2) For possession/ownership ('He has a new house' / 'He has got a new house'); 3) For enjoyment/activity ('I took a bath' -> 'I had a bath').
specialDifficulties: Distinguishing between causative, possession, and activity uses of 'have'.

title: Sold Out
keyStructures: Asking Permission ('Can/May I use your phone, please?'). Probability modals: 'May' vs. 'Might' ('Perhaps he will come tomorrow -> He may/might come tomorrow'). The phrase 'as well' ('I have nothing to do so I might come as well' - meaning 50/50 probability).
specialDifficulties: 'Interesting' (adjective) vs. 'Interested' (feeling/verb). 'It is' (contraction) vs. 'Its' (possessive). Differences between 'Realize' and 'Understand'.

title: One Man in a Boat
keyStructures: Gerunds: 1) As Subject ('Fishing is my hobby'); 2) As object of Preposition ('I told you that he was interested in cooking'); 3) For combining sentences ('He sat there without saying anything').
specialDifficulties: Distinguishing between Gerunds, Present Participles, and Infinitives.

title: Mad or Not?
keyStructures: Passive Voice with Modals / Auxiliary verbs: Object is not a person ('The chairs will be moved', 'The flight could have been delayed') vs. Subject is a person ('She could be loved by everyone', 'He must be accompanied by me').
specialDifficulties: Ensuring proper agent placement and modal passive forms.

title: A Glass Envelope
keyStructures: Verbs followed by prepositions: 'agree with', 'apologize for', 'believe in', 'depend on', 'listen to', 'look at', 'wait for', 'think of/about', etc.
specialDifficulties: Choosing the correct preposition based on the verb.

title: A New House
keyStructures: No specific key structures assigned. Focus is on review of all PP1-PP22 materials.
specialDifficulties: Integrating various structures harmoniously in communication.
